issues.description: Method parameter mismatch for Rideable.messageOnRide: The problem statement (UML and textual description) declares Rideable.messageOnRide() with no parameters and the template Main calls r.messageOnRide() with no arguments. The solution repository defines Rideable.messageOnRide(String equipment) (and Pig/Seal implement this signature). This divergence means students following the problem/template will implement or call a no-arg method, but the solution uses a one-argument signature, causing compilation/signature conflicts and blocking straightforward implementation or automated grading.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the messageOnRide signature across all artifacts. Two viable fixes: (A) Make the solution match the specification/template by changing Rideable.messageOnRide(String equipment) to messageOnRide() and update Pig/Seal implementations to return exactly "Riding on [Animal Type] [name]" (remove equipment usage), or (B) If an equipment parameter is intentional, update the problem statement UML and textual descriptions to declare messageOnRide(String equipment), and update the template Main to call r.messageOnRide("<equipment>") (provide an example equipment string) and adjust expected return text in the tasks accordingly. Choose one approach and apply consistently to problem_statement.md, template repository, and solution repository.

issues.description: The concept is the Rideable.messageOnRide method used to produce a ride message. In the problem statement and UML (problem_statement.md) the interface method is declared as messageOnRide():String and the template Main.java calls r.messageOnRide() with no arguments; the expected return format in the task text is "Riding on [Animal Type] [name]". In the solution repository, Rideable is declared with a different identifier/signature: messageOnRide(String equipment) (solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Rideable.java) and its implementations in Pig and Seal also require the equipment parameter and produce strings that include " with " + equipment (solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Pig.java and solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Seal.java). This is a naming/signature inconsistency: the same conceptual method is referenced with different signatures across artifacts, which will prevent students from mapping the requirement to the implementation and can cause compilation errors when using the template Main code or following the UML/text.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the method signature consistent across all artifacts. Option A (recommended to match problem/template): change the solution's Rideable interface to declare String messageOnRide(); and update Pig and Seal to implement messageOnRide() with no parameters and return the expected string format: "Riding on [Animal Type] [name]" (e.g., "Riding on Pig Doodle"). Also remove the 'equipment' parameter and any ' with ' + equipment fragments. Option B (alternate): if equipment is intentionally required, update the problem statement, UML, and template Main.java to declare and call messageOnRide(String equipment) and describe the equipment usage and expected return format consistently.
